requirements.title: Underscore has the underscore terminal
requirements.source: 6.1.4 R602 (J3/24-007 PDF page 67, printed page 53, line 25).
requirements.definition: The underscore syntax class is the single underscore character. Its use as an alphanumeric-character comes from R601; the permitted positions in a name come from R603. R602 does not define a kind suffix, allow an initial underscore in a name, or prescribe a processor character code.
requirements.oracle: A short name containing the underscore terminal and the corresponding name without it denote two separately assigned integer objects. Check both values so silently discarding the underscore cannot satisfy this admission control.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This is a positive control, not independent rejection coverage for invalid names or literal-kind syntax. Those grammars retain their existing owners. A substituted special character would also violate the enclosing grammar and is not used as a second R602 negative. Graphic appearance is separately pending under S6.1.1-001. Required diagnostic capability under 4.2 p2(3) does not mandate fatal rejection or a particular diagnostic code.
requirements.dependencies: 4.1.1 p1 treats the terminal literally (PDF page 44); 4.2 p2(3) establishes syntax diagnostic capability (PDF page 46). 6.1.1/R601 and 6.2.2/R603/C601 provide the legal short-name context (PDF pages 67-68).

review_rationale: Coordinator review independent of the draft authors; see doc/source_audits/lexical_batch_003.json. The terminal is admitted in a legal short name and is distinguished from omission of that terminal. R603 keeps ownership of initial-position and name-grammar restrictions.
